plain_english: Place, entry, form, and mark, and sign indeed; raising, awakening, and wheel-rest indeed — and
sanskrit_cite: sthānaṃ praveśo rūpaṃ ca lakṣaṃ lakṣaṇameva ca / utthāpanaṃ bodhanaṃ ca cakraviśrāmameva ca

plain_english: the arrival at the stage, and the final state indeed; rest, transformation, and the return indeed — and
sanskrit_cite: bhūmikāgamanaṃ caiva antāvasthā tathaiva ca / viśrāmaḥ pariṇāmaśca tathāgamanameva ca

plain_english: So the doctrine is thirteenfold: the supreme Śākta wisdom, pointed out in every Trika treatise by Śambhu himself.
sanskrit_cite: iti trayodaśavidhaṃ śāktaṃ vijñānamuttamam / sarveṣu trikaśāstreṣu sūcitaṃ śambhunā svayam

plain_english: Five fingers below the navel, two fingers above the member — between them lies the place called the bulb, remembered as the station of the wheel.
sanskrit_cite: nābhyadho 'ṅgulāḥ pañca meḍhrasyordhvāṅguladvayam / tanmadhye kandanāmā ca cakrasthānamiti smṛtam

plain_english: Hold the breath in and out, and cast the mind right there; master the currents of wind completely, and lead them until they enter the middle.
sanskrit_cite: prāṇāpānanirodhena manastatraiva niḥkṣipet / samyag vāyugatiṃ jitvā yāvan madhyagatāṃ nayet

plain_english: This — they say — is entry. Now I will tell the form: a wheel like a horned pond, six-spoked, and steady beyond.
sanskrit_cite: eṣa praveśa ity āhū rūpaṃ vakṣyāmi cādhunā / śṛṅgāṭakanibhaṃ cakraṃ ṣaḍaraṃ cāparaṃ dhruvam

plain_english: The bulb glows like a pomegranate blossom, red by its very nature; this form is declared the third — it consists of contemplation.
sanskrit_cite: dāḍimīkusumaprakhyaṃ kandaṃ vai jātilohitam / etadrūpaṃ samākhyātaṃ tṛtīyaṃ cintanātmakam

plain_english: Set the mind in that middle until it stands steady there; when the wind's hold is released, point out the mark.
sanskrit_cite: tanmadhye nikṣipec cittaṃ yāvat tatra sthirīkṛtam / tyaktaruddho yadā vāyustadā lakṣaṃ vinirdiśet

plain_english: In the middle of the bulb-wheel stands a digit of the unstruck sound, ringed with lines above and below, coiled like a serpent.
sanskrit_cite: kandacakrasya madhyasthā tv anāhatamayī kalā / adhaūrdhve rekhāsaṃyuktā bhujaṃgakuṭilākṛtiḥ

plain_english: Above and below abides her state — sun and moon both; truly she shines, bright as a thousand suns.
sanskrit_cite: ūrdhvādho 'vasthitāvasthā sūryācandramasāv ubhau / satyaṃ virājamānā sā sahasrārkasamaprabhā
